        "contents": "    private func updateMutualState(targetDeviceId: String) {\n        // Find the newest visitor entry for the target device\n        let targetVisits = cachedVisitorHistory.filter { $0.DeviceID.uppercased() == targetDeviceId.uppercased() }\n        guard let newestVisit = targetVisits.max(by: { $0.TimeStampDate &lt; $1.TimeStampDate }) else {\n            // No visits from target device, not mutual\n            isMutualNavigation = false\n            return\n        }\n        \n        let age = Date().timeIntervalSince(newestVisit.TimeStampDate)\n        \n        // Hysteresis: different thresholds for enter/exit\n        if isMutualNavigation {\n            // Currently mutual: exit if age &gt;= T_exit\n            isMutualNavigation = age &lt;= tExit\n        } else {\n            // Not currently mutual: enter if age &lt;= T_enter\n            isMutualNavigation = age &lt;= tEnter\n        }\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "    private func calculateRoute(ignoreCache: Bool = false) {\n        // Calculate a new route between user and selected device.\n        // Prefers a cached route when movement &lt; 100m; applies a daily network request limit.\n        guard let user = userCoordinate, let device = deviceCoordinate else { return }\n        // Try to reuse cached route first unless explicitly told to ignore cache\n        if !ignoreCache {\n            if useCachedRouteIfValid() { return }\n            // Only recalc when one of the positions changed since the last route calculation (or if there's no route yet)\n            let userTimestampChanged = userTimestamp != lastRouteUserTimestamp\n            let deviceTimestampChanged = deviceTimestamp != lastRouteDeviceTimestamp\n            var userCoordinatesChanged = true\n            if let lastUser = lastRouteUserCoordinate {\n                userCoordinatesChanged = (lastUser.latitude != user.latitude) || (lastUser.longitude != user.longitude)\n            }\n            var deviceCoordinatesChanged = true\n            if let lastDevice = lastRouteDeviceCoordinate {\n                deviceCoordinatesChanged = (lastDevice.latitude != device.latitude) || (lastDevice.longitude != device.longitude)\n            }\n            let transportTypeChanged = settings.navigationTransportType != lastRouteTransportType\n            let shouldRecalculate = (route == nil) || userTimestampChanged || deviceTimestampChanged || userCoordinatesChanged || deviceCoordinatesChanged || transportTypeChanged\n            if !shouldRecalculate { return }\n        }\n\n        // Enforce daily limit through centralized counter with calendar-day reset\n        routeCounter.checkAndResetIfNeeded()\n        guard routeCounter.count &lt; routeRequestDailyLimit else {\n            showErrorOverlay(\n                \"Daily route request limit reached\",",

        "contents": "    private func handleIncomingURL(_ url: URL) {\n        guard url.scheme == \"miataru\" else { return }\n        let deviceID = (url.host ?? \"\").uppercased()\n        guard !deviceID.isEmpty else { return }\n\n        Task { @MainActor in\n            // When resuming from background, SwiftUI may restore navigation state after the URL\n            // event is delivered. Deferring slightly ensures the deep link wins over restoration.\n            await Task.yield()\n            try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 180_000_000)\n\n            // If the device already exists, navigate to it; otherwise fall back to add flow.\n            if KnownDeviceStore.shared.devices.contains(where: { $0.DeviceID == deviceID }) {\n                showAddDeviceSheet = false\n                pendingDeviceID = nil\n                SettingsManager.shared.lastOpenedDeviceID = deviceID\n            } else {\n                pendingDeviceID = deviceID\n                showAddDeviceSheet = true\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nprivate struct DeviceWindowEntrypoint: View {\n    @Binding var deviceID: String?\n    @Environment(\\.openWindow) private var openWindow\n    @Environment(\\.dismissWindow) private var dismissWindow\n\n    init(deviceID: Binding&lt;String?&gt;) {\n        self._deviceID = deviceID\n    }\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Group {\n            if let id = deviceID {\n                iPad_DeviceMapView(deviceID: id)\n            } else {\n                Text(NSLocalizedString(\"no_device_selected\", comment: \"No device selected for this window.\"))\n            }\n        }\n        .task {\n            if LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation {\n                LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation = false\n                openWindow(id: \"main\")\n                if let id = deviceID {\n                    dismissWindow(value: id)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "        }\n    }\n    \n    private func checkAutoStopCondition() {\n        // Automatically stop navigation if devices are within 50m of each other,\n        // but only if they weren't already within 50m when navigation started\n        // Skip check if navigation has already been stopped\n        guard !navigationStopped else { return }\n        guard let user = userCoordinate, let device = deviceCoordinate else { return }\n        guard let initialDist = initialDistance else {\n            // If initial distance hasn't been recorded yet, record it now\n            recordInitialDistance()\n            return\n        }\n        \n        let userLocation = CLLocation(latitude: user.latitude, longitude: user.longitude)\n        let deviceLocation = CLLocation(latitude: device.latitude, longitude: device.longitude)\n        let currentDistance = userLocation.distance(from: deviceLocation)\n        \n        // Only auto-stop if:\n        // 1. Current distance is within threshold (50m)\n        // 2. Initial distance was greater than threshold (devices were not already close)\n        if currentDistance &lt;= autoStopDistanceThreshold &amp;&amp; initialDist &gt; autoStopDistanceThreshold {\n            // Devices have moved close to each other, stop navigation automatically\n            // Mark navigation as stopped to prevent re-triggering\n            navigationStopped = true\n            // Show info overlay and trigger haptics\n            Haptic.notifySuccess()\n            infoOverlayManager.show(\n                message: NSLocalizedString(\"navigation_stopped_automatically\", comment: \"Navigation stopped automatically - devices are close\"),\n                duration: 6.0\n            )\n            // Stop navigation but keep the map view showing both devices\n            stopNavigation()\n        }\n    }\n    \n    private func stopNavigation() {\n        // Stop navigation without dismissing the view",

        "contents": "    private func pollVisitorHistory() async {\n        guard let targetId = targetDeviceId,\n              let url = URL(string: serverURL) else {\n            return\n        }\n        \n        do {\n            let visitors = try await MiataruAPIClient.getVisitorHistory(\n                serverURL: url,\n                forDeviceID: ourDeviceId,\n                amount: 100  // Get enough entries to find recent visits\n            )\n            \n            await MainActor.run {\n                // Update cached history if it changed (compare by count and device IDs)\n                let hasChanged = visitors.count != cachedVisitorHistory.count ||\n                    !visitors.allSatisfy { visitor in\n                        cachedVisitorHistory.contains { $0.DeviceID == visitor.DeviceID &amp;&amp; $0.TimeStamp == visitor.TimeStamp }\n                    }\n                if hasChanged {\n                    cachedVisitorHistory = visitors\n                }\n                // Always re-evaluate mutual state based on current time, even if history hasn't changed.\n                // This ensures the state updates when the age of the last visit exceeds the exit threshold.\n                updateMutualState(targetDeviceId: targetId)\n                lastPollTime = Date()\n            }\n        } catch {\n            debugLog(\"[MutualNavigationDetector] Failed to fetch visitor history: \\(error)\")\n            // On error, still re-evaluate state based on cached data since time is passing\n            await MainActor.run {\n                if let targetId = targetDeviceId {\n                    updateMutualState(targetDeviceId: targetId)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    \n    /// Update mutual navigation state based on visitor history and hysteresis logic.\n    private func updateMutualState(targetDeviceId: String) {\n        // Find the newest visitor entry for the target device",

        "contents": "            .onChange(of: settings.lastOpenedDeviceID) { _, newDeviceID in\n                guard let deviceID = newDeviceID,\n                      store.devices.contains(where: { $0.DeviceID == deviceID }) else { return }\n                let requestedID = deviceID\n                Task { @MainActor in\n                    // If we’re already showing the requested device (normal in-app navigation),\n                    // do nothing to avoid a visible pop/push animation.\n                    if navigationPath.last == requestedID {\n                        return\n                    }\n\n                    // Clear first, then set after a short delay to override any restored navigation state.\n                    navigationPath = []\n                    await Task.yield()\n                    try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 180_000_000)\n                    // Guard against a stale delayed task (e.g. multiple widget taps).\n                    guard settings.lastOpenedDeviceID == requestedID else { return }\n                    navigationPath = [requestedID]\n                }\n            }\n            // Intentionally do not reset didAutoNavigateFromSavedDevice on\n            // changes to lastOpenedDeviceID to avoid unintended re-pushes\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#Preview {\n    let store = KnownDeviceStore.shared\n    store.devices = [\n        KnownDevice(name: \"iPhone 13\", deviceID: UUID().uuidString, color: .red),\n        KnownDevice(name: \"iPad Pro\", deviceID: UUID().uuidString, color: .green),\n        KnownDevice(name: \"MacBook Air\", deviceID: UUID().uuidString, color: .blue)\n    ]\n    return iPhone_DevicesView().environmentObject(store)\n}",

        "contents": "    private func calculateRoute(ignoreCache: Bool = false) {\n        // Calculate a new route between user and selected device.\n        // Prefers a cached route when movement &lt; 100m; applies a daily network request limit.\n        guard let user = userCoordinate, let device = deviceCoordinate else { return }\n        // Try to reuse cached route first unless explicitly told to ignore cache\n        if !ignoreCache {\n            if useCachedRouteIfValid() { return }\n            // Only recalc when one of the positions changed since the last route calculation (or if there's no route yet)\n            let userTimestampChanged = userTimestamp != lastRouteUserTimestamp\n            let deviceTimestampChanged = deviceTimestamp != lastRouteDeviceTimestamp\n            var userCoordinatesChanged = true\n            if let lastUser = lastRouteUserCoordinate {\n                userCoordinatesChanged = (lastUser.latitude != user.latitude) || (lastUser.longitude != user.longitude)\n            }\n            var deviceCoordinatesChanged = true\n            if let lastDevice = lastRouteDeviceCoordinate {\n                deviceCoordinatesChanged = (lastDevice.latitude != device.latitude) || (lastDevice.longitude != device.longitude)\n            }\n            let transportTypeChanged = settings.navigationTransportType != lastRouteTransportType\n            let shouldRecalculate = (route == nil) || userTimestampChanged || deviceTimestampChanged || userCoordinatesChanged || deviceCoordinatesChanged || transportTypeChanged\n            if !shouldRecalculate { return }\n        }\n\n        // Enforce daily limit through centralized counter with calendar-day reset\n        routeCounter.checkAndResetIfNeeded()\n        guard routeCounter.count &lt; routeRequestDailyLimit else {\n            showErrorOverlay(\n                \"Daily route request limit reached\",",

        "contents": "        }\n\n        return result\n    }\n\n    func polylineSegments(from entries: [MiataruLocationData], maxGapMeters: Double = 5_000) -&gt; [[CLLocationCoordinate2D]] {\n        guard !entries.isEmpty else { return [] }\n        var segments: [[CLLocationCoordinate2D]] = []\n        var current: [CLLocationCoordinate2D] = []\n\n        var lastLocation: CLLocation?\n        for entry in entries {\n            let coord = CLLocationCoordinate2D(latitude: entry.Latitude, longitude: entry.Longitude)\n            let location = CLLocation(latitude: coord.latitude, longitude: coord.longitude)\n\n            if let last = lastLocation, location.distance(from: last) &gt; maxGapMeters, !current.isEmpty {\n                segments.append(current)\n                current = []\n            }\n\n            current.append(coord)\n            lastLocation = location\n        }\n\n        if !current.isEmpty {\n            segments.append(current)\n        }\n\n        return segments\n    }\n\n    private func lowerBound(for value: Double) -&gt; Int? ## The Problem

The route polyline wasn't updating when `mutualNavigationDetector.isMutualNavigation` changed. The Map's content builder wasn't observing the `@Published` property, so changes didn't trigger a re-render.

## The Solution

Created a separate `RoutePolylineView` helper view that uses `@ObservedObject` to observe `mutualNavigationDetector`. When `isMutualNavigation` changes, SwiftUI re-renders the view and updates the polyline display.

**Key changes:**
1. Extracted route polyline rendering into `RoutePolylineView`
2. Used `@ObservedObject` to observe `mutualNavigationDetector`
3. Passed required parameters (route, device info, timestamps, etc.)

When devices are mutually active during navigation, the route polyline now shows the additional semi-transparent overlay polyline (0.6 opacity, 2.5 line width) on top of the main polyline.

The fix is complete and ready to test. The polyline should update when mutual navigation state changes.

## Summary

The Map content builder wasn't observing changes to `mutualNavigationDetector.isMutualNavigation` because it's a `@Published` property on a `@StateObject`, and the Map content builder may not re-evaluate when that changes.

**The fix:**
1. Added a `@State` variable `isMutualNavigation` that tracks the mutual navigation state
2. Updated the `.onChange` handler to sync this state when `mutualNavigationDetector.isMutualNavigation` changes
3. Use the `@State` variable in the Map content builder instead of directly accessing the detector
4. Initialize the state when the view appears and when the device changes

When `mutualNavigationDetector.isMutualNavigation` changes:
- The `.onChange` handler updates `isMutualNavigation`
- The `@State` change triggers SwiftUI to re-evaluate the Map content
- The polyline display updates to show/hide the additional overlay polyline

The code should compile and the route polyline should update when devices become mutually active during navigation.

Added an `.id()` modifier to the Map that includes the mutual navigation state to force re-evaluation when it changes. Also preserving the camera position to avoid resetting it.

**Summary of the fix:**
1. Using the `@State` variable `isMutualNavigation` in the Map content (synced with `mutualNavigationDetector.isMutualNavigation`)
2. Added an `.id()` modifier to the Map that includes `isMutualNavigation` to force re-evaluation
3. Preserving and restoring the camera position when the mutual navigation state changes to prevent camera reset

When `mutualNavigationDetector.isMutualNavigation` changes:
- The `.onChange` handler updates `isMutualNavigation`
- The Map's `.id()` changes, forcing the Map content to re-evaluate
- The camera position is preserved to avoid resetting
- The overlay polyline appears or disappears based on the mutual navigation state

The polyline should now update when devices become mutually active. The overlay polyline (semi-transparent, thinner) should appear on top of the main polyline when both devices are navigating to each other.

Updated the visual change for mutual navigation.

**What should change visually:**

When devices are mutually active (both navigating to each other), an orange overlay polyline appears on top of the main route polyline.

**Before (not visible):**
- Overlay used the same color (blue/green) with reduced opacity (0.6)
- Very subtle and hard to notice

**After (visible):**
- Overlay uses orange (`RouteStyle.mutualNavigation`)
- Line width is 3px (thinner than the main 4px line, but visible)
- Creates a clear double-line effect: the main blue/green route with an orange overlay on top

**Visual states:**
- Normal navigation: Single blue/green polyline (4px width)
- Mutual navigation: Blue/green polyline (4px) + orange overlay polyline (3px) on top

The orange overlay indicates both devices are navigating to each other. If it’s still not visible, we can:
1. Make the overlay thicker (e.g., 3.5px)
2. Use a different color (purple, red, etc.)
3. Use a dashed line style for the overlay
4. Add a pulsing animation

Test it and let me know if you want any adjustments.

All changes have been committed. Summary:

## Summary of Changes

**Problem fixed:**
- Route polyline didn't update when devices became mutually active during navigation
- Map was reloading when mutual navigation state changed

**Solution implemented:**

1. **State management** (`iPhone_DeviceNavigationView.swift`):
   - Added `@State private var isMutualNavigation: Bool = false` to track mutual navigation state
   - Synced with `mutualNavigationDetector.isMutualNavigation` via `.onChange` handler
   - Ensures Map content builder observes state changes

2. **Visual indicator** (`RouteStyle.swift`):
   - Added `RouteStyle.mutualNavigation` color (orange) for the overlay polyline
   - Provides clear visual distinction from the main route

3. **Route polyline rendering** (`iPhone_DeviceNavigationView.swift`):
   - Updated all route polyline rendering paths to conditionally show orange overlay
   - Overlay is 2.5px width (thinner than main 4px polyline)
   - Applies to all route states: remaining, completed, and progress segments

4. **Performance optimization**:
   - Removed `.id()` modifier that was causing full map reloads
   - Map now smoothly adds/removes overlay polyline without reloading
   - Camera position and map state remain unchanged during updates

**Result:**
When devices are mutually active, an orange overlay polyline appears on top of the main route polyline, providing clear visual feedback without map reloads or camera resets.

Commit created: `ca96cb4`
